chunks.arabic_text: ثَلَاثَةٌ - سَعِيدُ بْنُ خَثِيمٍ، أَبُو مُعَمَّرٍ الْهَلَالِيُّ - وَأَخُوهُ مُعَمَّرٌ -.

translations.en: Three – Saʿīd ibn Khuthaym, Abū MuʿAmmār al-Hilālī – and his brother Muʿammar.

chunks.arabic_text: كَانَ سَعِيدٌ زَيْدِيًّا، وَحَدِيثُهُ فِي أَحَادِيثِ أَصْحَابِنَا، وَهُوَ تَابِعِيٌّ - عَلَى مَا زَعَمَ - يَرْوِي عَنْ جَدِّهِ لِأُمِّهِ عُبَيْدَةَ بْنِ عُمَرَ الْكِلَابِيِّ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ). وَرَوَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ). وَهُوَ ضَعِيفٌ جِدًّا، لَا يُرْتَفَعُ بِهِ.

translations.en: Saʿīd was a Zaydī. His ḥadīth are amongst the ḥadīths of our companions. He was a tabiʿī – upon what is claimed – narrating from his maternal grandfather ʿUbayda ibn ʿUmar al-Kilābī from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He narrated from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) and Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon them). He is very weak, and one does not ascend by him.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafa* highlights Saʿīd ibn Khuthaym, a Zaydī tabiʿī whose narrations from the Prophet and the Imams are considered unreliable due to his specific sectarian affiliation. The designation 'very weak' (daʿī jiddan) indicates that his reports are not elevated to the level of strong evidence in Shia jurisprudence, reflecting the historical scrutiny of Zaydī narrators within the broader Shia scholarly tradition.
en.seo_question: Who is Sa'id ibn Khuthaym and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ جِدًّا: Very weak (a technical term for low reliability)
key_terms.لَا يُرْتَفَعُ بِهِ: One does not ascend by him (his narrations are not elevated to Sahih or Hasan status)
